name: LingBot-Map
plain: LingBot-Map (Robbyant, 2026): streaming 3D reconstruction, cameras and depth for a long image sequence frame by frame with a sliding-window cache. Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: LingBot-Map (Robbyant, 2026): streaming 3D reconstruction. A VGGT-style aggregator (DINOv2 ViT-L patch embed, 24 frame / global attention blocks, 3D RoPE) runs causally over the views in order with a KV cache (scale frames + a sliding window), then a camera head and a DPT depth head give cameras and depth of every view.

papers.title: LingBot-Map: Geometric Context Transformer for Streaming 3D Reconstruction

limitations: On the RTX 5060 Ti reference input, stream=True reduced peak allocated memory across loading and inference from 3,591 to 2,532 MiB portable and 3,798 to 2,643 MiB kernels. Depth, confidence and camera outputs matched exactly.

On CUDA, stream=True keeps the 24 pairs of aggregator blocks in host RAM. Each new view after the initial scale frames transfers those weights again. The camera, depth head and attention cache stay on the GPU.
With streamed weights, the portable FP32 benchmark on 24 synthetic 320 x 448 input views takes 10.61 s and peaks at 9,128 MiB allocated and 9,572 MiB reserved on the RTX 5060 Ti.
Views are a sequence (a video): each view only sees the first `scale_frames` views and the views before it (older than `window` frames: their 6 special tokens only). At most 1024 views.
task_io: Input: several images of one scene (posed and calibrated for multi-view stereo, unposed otherwise). Output: depth maps and, where the model predicts them, cameras and 3-D points.

variants.name: lingbot-map

licence.training_note: Per the README: a stage-1 bidirectional (VGGT-style) checkpoint, then streaming training; datasets are not listed

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 1, resized or padded inside the model

portable.protocol: Median of two rounds of five synchronized calls after two warm-ups. Only the timed input is resident.
portable.note: Released the causal cache before the final depth head. Both synthetic sequences and five labeled scenes were bitwise identical.

original16.protocol: median of 3 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: the authors' mixed-precision option (bfloat16); upstream GCTStream.inference_streaming (demo defaults, SDPA), bfloat16 aggregator

kernels.protocol: Median of two rounds of five synchronized calls after two warm-ups. Only the timed input is resident.
kernels.note: Released the causal cache before the final depth head. Both synthetic sequences and five labeled scenes were bitwise identical.

quality.title: DTU scans 1, 9, 24, 33, 75, view 24 + 7 sources, AbsRel / delta1 %
quality.protocol: 640x512 crops, the 7 most co-visible views as sources. Ground truth is depth rendered from the structured-light points. AbsRel / delta1 over GT pixels, after per-image median scaling unless the model takes the cameras (calibrated MVS: cameras, error in mm; PatchMatchNet also the depth range 425-935 mm, MVSAnywhere its own range from the camera baselines).

quality.title: DTU (five scans), view 24 + 7 sources at 480 x 640, AbsRel / delta1 %
quality.protocol: Scans 1, 9, 24, 33 and 75. Use view 24 and its seven best paired views, resize to 480 x 640, and align the reference depth by median scale before averaging the scans.

portable.note: Reference view 24 and seven co-visible sources. Median-scale aligned depth.

compile.note: Reference view 24 and seven co-visible sources. Median-scale aligned depth.

input.name: motorcycle
input.title: Motorcycle, Middlebury 2014 stereo (left and right view, downscaled 4x)

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.02 and p99 <= 0.25 (absolute error of the output `depth`).
